description: A black-and-white collie lies flat in the shed doorway with its chin on its paws, small at the far end of the frame, on duty and ignoring the entire racket.
A tabby barn cat is curled into the spare corner of the lamb crate, small and half-buried, having decided this is now a cat bed.
A robin sits small on the top rail of a hurdle at the edge of the frame, head cocked, waiting for the straw to be turned over.
A speckled hen has walked in and is standing small on top of a bale at the back of the shed, looking down on the pens with open disapproval.
A ginger cat is stretched out small along the top of the bale stack, one paw dangling over the edge above the pens.
A young collie sits small and upright just inside the door, tail going, plainly desperate to be allowed in and plainly not allowed in.
Two swallows have got in early and are small up in the rafters on the far beam, turning in the space above the pens.
A small brown hen is settled in the loose straw at the back of the shed, wings spread flat, taking a dust bath in someone else's bedding.
A collie lies small and low in the wet grass well off to one side, belly down, eyes locked on the mob and moving nothing but its eyebrows.
A jackdaw walks small along the top of the stone wall behind the flock, stopping now and then to look sideways at the whole business.
A brown hare sits small and bolt upright in the far corner of the field, ears flat, having badly misjudged when to cross.
A small tabby cat is threaded up onto the top bar of the field gate, sitting where nothing can step on it.
A pair of rooks stand small on a molehill at the back of the field, taking turns to pull at the fresh soil.
An old grey pony watches small over the wall from the next field, chin resting on the top stones.
A pied wagtail runs small along the muddy rim of the trough, tail pumping, picking at the churned edge.
A small white goose has appointed itself to the gateway and is standing in the mud there, wings half out, refusing to move for anybody.
